I recently finished Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software, the classic by the Gang of Four. What stayed with me was the experience of recognizing familiar design problems—and finding a more structured way to think about them.

For someone still building experience in software design, that recognition makes the book rewarding. Some ideas initially feel like a refresher. As the discussion develops, they become connected to larger questions about how a system is organized and how its parts work together.

From fundamentals to a vocabulary for design

The opening discussion revisits object-oriented design fundamentals and puts them to work in an example. Seeing several patterns participate in the same design gives the reader a reason to care about the individual patterns before studying them in detail.
